items.note: Association named; 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose president 1889-1911; creamery 1891.
Article VII: paid on butterfat by test, not weight; station test governs.
'under payment by weight, nothing that followed would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Teague as bookkeeper and Sill as Larrow Green buttermaker; Loomis named. List-type item, so the core fact is enough.
Son is right, but Section A says Selby Vose became manager in 1911 (the planted error); key says 1913.
Station-gain line given with its shape: credited vs received, 5 1/4%, carried to general account. Run dates the column from 1897, not 1898; the bold gates only the line.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, 7 miles, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, tested; charge for which bottle neck is ruled; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice table: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, tester, freight, $77.93.
'0.19 ... flat in every month and season'; 'same proportion, every time, in every season.'
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Station test book in Keddie's hand, 4 May 1896 to 31 Dec 1924.
Both figures in Section A: 1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass and 3.61 on the station glass.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, question mark.
Wife Orra, Emmet Brant's sister; Emmet had the largest farm.
1919 circular is present, but Section A lacks Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why. Both bolded parts are required.
Died February 1934; book impounded 1925, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 Jan 1897; the two scales always agreed.
Conflates the two gaps: 'The Hollow tested 0.19 below the valley' in the 1902 complaint passage. E#11 also rejects Roy's 0.17 in favor of 0.19.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908; hay conclusion reported as its finding.
200,000 lb at 3.42 in 1910; error stated as proportional.
Roy Brant lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958; to Hazel in 1962.
Jerome Cudd's cheese company at Alder Corners, Vessey County, over the ridge (Redlow not named). Founding year declared unsettled; 1913 not asserted.
From 1915, four Bottom men hauled there in the summer flush and to the station the rest of the year.
Other county (Vessey), his own glass, and Jerome never compared his figures: more than two elements.
Same cows read 3.80 over the ridge and 3.61 at the station. Run's own overlap recount (8/10 seasons) is unbolded context.
Same cows, same Bottom, same seasons, different readings: 'not the land or the men'; hay theory answered.
Rosalie, daughter, took over in 1941 and had the figures copied for Ivy in 1958.
Section A names Strawn and the Ordell circuit but gives no 1907 start, only retirement in 1936. The run's 'from 1908' is in Section F only.
Strawn's lactometer and his never finding water are absent from Section A (they appear only in F).
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
'Strawn wrote down the condemnation and drew no inference about the 26 years behind it.'
Order 28 June, reply 2 July, new glass July 1923, 1924 at 3.80; office treated it as 'a broken window'.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state office, then the college library in 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick; 17 March to 4 May 1925; second and third sittings in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); 'no cause established'.
Four books listed; Strawn's notebook recorded the condemnation and nobody laid it beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April, before the finding of 'no cause'; $3,800 'without admission', charged to station account.
Award one fifth of the loss; charged to the station account that carried the station-gain line.
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, dairy husbandry graduate student at Farland, with Vaught.
Lists items she gathered but never makes the point that the records had never been in the same room.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.95 (0.88 appears only in C, but this is a list-type core fact).
3.61/0.95 = 3.80, one part in twenty, 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923.
40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and it 'sits in the ledgers as station gain'.
Bulletin 471, Oct 1958 is given, but of the bolded intervals only '24 years after his death' appears; 35 and 33 are missing.
Granddaughter, derived through Duncan.
Second cousins with derivation; full vs half siblings left open, generation count unchanged.
Gideon, father; Article VII made the station test govern, and the son enforced it.
Headline 'the best evidence says none' and E#32 'Resolution: no connection': A01 asserted. Also treats a family denial as outranking, where the key says it is not a record.
$19,000; one fifth.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5% of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 with the sum shown.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part-year reason given.
1896 intake cannot be determined (A02 abstained).
Variable: the measuring glass or pipette.
Tester, herds, pasture, scales, bottles, acid held constant.
Nine weeks at 3.80, back to 3.61 when the station glass returned.
Rules out tester, water and land; limits: not how much short, not which piece.
Ledger surplus (Kyle), 1911 interval (Orra/Falke), 1924 glass (Keddie's averages).
Independence argued; all hold without the 1958 measurement.
'Did the bookkeeper ever question it? No.' A09 asserted.
Answers the literal question 'No ... Selby Vose did not know'; key says yes, he knew the station tested low (1902 grievance, 1919 circular).
Signed ledger sheets with station gain, 1919 circular, argued water in 1925: three of the five.
Verdict 'did not know ... negligence, not knowing concealment' asserts A03; later hedging does not undo it.
E.g. weigh book 1897 (document), 1908 Jan-Mar (report vs letter), 1924 at 3.80 (arithmetic), six farms, crate in loft.
NT-11 12 July (Vose, Rundle; 28 June order), NT-1 16.27 (Vaught, Chronicle; 0.95 fit), NT-14 $77.39 (Ammon, Chronicle; line items).
A04 and A10 correctly abstained; A06 resolved as 'Larrow Green'.
Grigg's letter vs report, Duncan's 1868 vs 82 in 1948, Ammon's 'before 1900', Nym's swapped keepers.
16.72/17.6 = 95%, proportional; onset 1897 after 3.80 in 1896; end 12 June 1923, 3.80 in 1924; farms unchanged.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by lactometer, cheese yields, heavy cream, 1911/1924.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavier, plus the 1911 interval and 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter, nil in summer, vs a flat 0.19.
'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' A07 asserted.
'Ansel Keddie suspected the glass'; Frick's account 'rejected'. A05 asserted.
150 words counted by whitespace tokens (including '&'); at the limit, not over it.
Invoice, weigh book, ledger, cheese-factory tests, inspector's notebook, test book: at least five.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.
